narration: We begin with the existing method, shown in the blue panel. The legend defines two operations used throughout: a circled minus for the absolute difference, and a circled dot for concatenation.
In the first stage, an input image x is passed through a diffusion model, which reconstructs it as x prime.
Crucially, the two stages are separated. The first stage and the second stage are trained without interaction.
The second stage takes x and x prime, computes their absolute difference, and produces the reconstruction error map x rec.
A classifier reads that error map and decides whether the image is real or generated.
Our method, in the yellow panel, replaces this split pipeline with end-to-end training.
Two inputs are used: the image x and its pseudo counterpart x pse. An FMRE module fuses their features and conditions a single shared diffusion model.
The diffusion model emits two reconstructions, x prime and x pse prime. Because the branches share training signal, they achieve better alignment with the inputs.
Each input is compared with its own reconstruction by absolute difference, yielding two error maps: x rec and x pse rec.
The two error maps are concatenated and fed to the classifier, which outputs the final real or generated decision, all optimized jointly end to end.
